Fouta Djallon was a Muslim theocratic state born of the 1720s jihad; Timbo was occupied by French troops in 1896. France's ruling class was Catholic under the Concordat regime (until 1905), then secular; it never adopted Islam, only co-opted Muslim chiefs administratively.

Theravada Buddhism 'took deep root' in Ayutthaya (with Brahmanical court ritual); Theravada dominant in Cambodia by the 13th-14th centuries. Naresuan captured Lovek in 1594; both sides Theravada Buddhist.

Rabih was 'a Muslim military leader' who took Bornu in 1893, sacked Kuka and ruled from Dikwa with a centralized administration. Kanem-Bornu had been an Islamic state since its ruler Umme converted in the late 11th century. Arabic literacy assumed for Rabih's administration.
